source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-105: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 105 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For this cluster_design case, treat the platform as unverified until inventory and traces establish the node/GPU/NIC topology, affinity, PCIe/NVLink paths, firmware and software versions, MTU, transport, registration permissions, GPU-direct support, message-size distribution, concurrency, clocks, and workload; mark unknowns explicitly. Explain the data path from the training or inference framework through the communication library, RDMA verbs work requests and completions, registered host or GPU memory, queue pairs, NIC/link, and peer endpoint. RDMA can avoid host copies and reduce CPU involvement, but GPU-direct, transport choice, and fallback must be measured rather than assumed. Define a falsifiable hypothesis before changing configuration: for the same workload and interleaved matched non-RDMA control, the verified RDMA path reduces p50 and p95 communication time by at least 10% while not increasing p99 step time, CPU saturation, retries, timeouts, link errors, error rate, or application-level correctness failures. Report sample counts, warm-up, randomization, units, confidence intervals or bootstrap uncertainty, and separate end-to-end step time, communication and overlap time, throughput, bandwidth, p50/p95/p99 latency, completion latency, queue occupancy, CPU/GPU utilization, retries, timeouts, and relevant NIC/GPU counters; do not infer application benefit from a device counter alone. For investigation or implementation, collect read-only topology and interface/verbs capabilities, correlate timestamps across framework, library, completion, and device telemetry, and preserve command output and configuration provenance without exposing secrets. Test host-staged and GPU-direct paths separately, verify registration and protection behavior, and use a small correctness-checked workload before scaling. A link failure or registration/transport error must trigger bounded retries and an explicit host-staged or non-RDMA fallback with alarms; stop or roll back if correctness fails, error/timeout rates exceed the predeclared limit, or the performance hypothesis is not met. Do not claim a causal improvement until the baseline, confounders, and independent evidence are recorded.
risks: RDMA and GPU-direct capabilities, topology, and fallback behavior are platform-dependent and unverified.
Device counters can be misinterpreted as end-to-end application benefit.
A link failure or retry storm can silently worsen tail latency or correctness.
evidence_required: node/GPU/NIC topology and affinity inventory
software, firmware, MTU, transport, registration and GPU-direct capability evidence
interleaved matched baseline and workload-distribution details
timestamp-correlated application, verbs/completion, NIC, GPU, error, and link telemetry
correctness results plus predeclared rollback thresholds and fallback test
